one_liner: TranscriptAPI.com is a hosted service that retrieves existing YouTube captions as timestamped text or JSON and helps agents discover videos through search, channels, and playlists.

auth.notes: The REST API uses a vendor-issued API key sent as a Bearer credential. OAuth 2.1 is documented for MCP, not for REST.

access.notes: New accounts receive 100 free credits without a payment card and can obtain an API key from the dashboard. The similarly named open-source Python package is separate from the hosted service.

api.notes: The read-only API supports transcript retrieval, YouTube search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. Transcript retrieval requires an existing caption track; the API does not transcribe raw audio.

mcp.notes: The vendor-hosted server offers 12 tools, supports OAuth 2.1 or API-key authentication, and shares the REST API account and credits.

verdict.rationale: Developers can use free self-serve credits or the vendor’s hosted MCP server to discover YouTube videos and retrieve existing captions. The read-only API cannot generate missing transcripts or manage YouTube content.

evidence.quote: The API uses Bearer token authentication. Include your API key in the Authorization header of every request:
100 free credits to try the API — no card required.
You can start for free: new accounts get 100 free credits, no card required, and one transcript costs one credit.
Get YouTube video transcripts through our REST API or seamlessly integrate with AI assistants using Model Context Protocol (MCP).
TranscriptAPI is a hosted REST API, separate from the open-source YouTubeTranscriptApi Python package, which fetches transcripts from your own machine.

The YouTube Transcript API provides a simple and reliable way to extract transcripts from YouTube videos programmatically. This complete reference covers authentication, request parameters, response formats, and practical examples.
TranscriptAPI is managed and also adds YouTube search, channel browsing and playlist extraction.

TranscriptAPI runs a hosted (remote) MCP server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp . Add that URL to an MCP client and your AI assistant can fetch YouTube transcripts, search YouTube, and list a channel’s or playlist’s videos.

Retrieve and store captions for one video or a bounded batch, read job and batch status, access stored transcripts and languages, and resolve playlist or channel video metadata through the YouTube Transcript REST API.
Read one transcript job's current processing, completed, failed, or requires-ASR-confirmation state without creating work or waiting.
List, fetch, translate, and delete your stored transcripts, and list async jobs. All endpoints accept the same API-key auth.

problems: Composio does not disclose the toolkit’s upstream hostname in its public listing, and compatibility with a TranscriptAPI.com key was not verified. The toolkit’s stored transcripts and asynchronous jobs match documentation for the separate YouTubeTranscript.dev service.
The billing page did not load directly. Free access was documented in the public pricing FAQ and MCP documentation. No authenticated API or MCP call was made.

verification.note: The quote documents an API key sent as a Bearer credential. It does not establish the note’s claim about OAuth for MCP.
New accounts receive free API credits without a card. The quotes do not show that keys are obtained from a dashboard.
The quotes establish a public REST API; the stated narrow breadth is not contradicted. They do not establish that it is read-only or requires existing captions.
The vendor says it runs a hosted MCP server that clients can use now. The tool count, authentication options, and shared credits in the note are not shown.
No claim was made, so there is nothing to check.

Free self-serve access and a documented API support buildability; the stated narrow breadth supports the caveat and main blocker. The rationale’s claims that the API is read-only and cannot generate missing transcripts are not established by the quotes.
